newsitem.title: UK: Romanian bank's debut Eurobond sells out.
newsitem.headline: Romanian bank's debut Eurobond sells out.

text.p: Romanian state bank Banca Comerciala Romana (BCR) launched a debut Eurobond on Tuesday and the $75 million three-year bond was quickly sold out.
"The BCR deal has gone very well," an official at lead manager Merrill Lynch said.
"Investor sentiment towards Romania has improved in recent weeks and this helped the deal. It has sold out," he said.

Romania plans to implement tough austerity measures to meet ambitious targets for reducing its budget deficit. A draft budget said the government aimed to cut the deficit to 4.5 percent of gross domestic product from 5.8 percent in 1996.
The BCR bond is the first dollar transaction from a Romanian borrower since the government launched its inaugural Eurobond in June of last year.
BCR priced the deal to yield three percentage points over U.S. Treasury notes.
"Romania's three-year bond, launched last year at 295 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, is now trading at 220 to 230 b.p.," the Merrill Lynch official said.
"The spread has come in by around 20 b.p. in the last few weeks as the perception of Romania has improved. This helped on the pricing of BCR," he said.

Romanian electricity company Renel is in the process of raising $100 million via a private placement. Merrill Lynch, also underwriter for the Renel transaction, declined to comment on the status of the deal. Bankers elsewhere said it could be completed this week.
Romania itself is expected to return to the capital markets this year. It needs to raise $3.0 billion of external debt, and plans to tap both the loan and bond markets.
Other borrowers eyeing the international bond market include the cities of Bucharest, Constanta and Brasov.
BCR, which specialised in industry financing before the 1989 fall of communism in Romania, was re-invented in December 1990. The bank continues to manage most loans to industry.

The bank is rated Ba3 by Moody's Investors Service and BB minus by Standard & Poor's, the same as Romania's sovereign foreign currency debt ratings. -- Aline van Duyn, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7748
